coherence.reasons: Both run the same sound hierarchy: market, then A, B and J against the board's limits, then gates. X's executive summary is tighter and each claim carries its evidence. But X has an internal tension: it says A 'passes every financial test in the plan case', then calls 25% the upside case and tells the board to plan on 30–32% ACoS, where its own table shows payback failing, while the verdict stays 'Recommended'. Its ACoS numbers also pull apart: target 28%, review at 30%, stop only above 32%, against a 28.6% break-even. Y's governing thought carries the condition ('if ad cost holds near 28%'), and its section findings, 28% ceiling and duty-adjusted 27% ceiling all follow from the 28.6% and 26.9% break-evens. Y's one loose end is the next step approving 'the $18M cap as a ceiling', which sits oddly beside a $1.9M cash low point.

judgment.reasons: Both reach the defensible conclusion: Amazon-led with gates, reject B on cap, payback and margin, defer Japan, raise the retail gate to 20%, and reset $40M. Y's gates are tied more closely to the board's payback constraint: a 28% quarterly ceiling, lowered to about 27% if the duty rises, with a stated action if missed (cut broad-keyword spend, slow the ramp). That directly weighs growth against payback. X's stop trigger fires only above 32% for two quarters, so ACoS sitting at 29–32% would miss payback without tripping anything. Its tariff checkpoint says to absorb the duty because 'the plan case still pays back', leaning on the 25% case it had already called upside. Y is also more candid on Japan: J returns more cash than A at any ACoS above about 25.9%, and the US is chosen for growth after 2030. X has real strengths Y lacks: a $4M cash envelope with a cumulative-cash stop, a 'what would change our view' section, and a door test before any retail rollout. Those keep the gap small.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the key figures accurately: $4.73 and $7.55 unit contributions, A at +2.4 / +0.4 / −2.3 across 25/28/32% ACoS, 28.6% break-even, B at −$20.8M peak and 4.5% margin, $26.4M and $37.6M 2030 revenue. Both challenge the 4.5 units per door, the 0.71 correlation and the $5.2B figure, and both caveat the four-brand competitor set. Y uses the critical evidence a little more fully: it shows the pilot-case-plus-duty result (−$0.7M), the 26.9% duty-adjusted break-even, B corrected for no halo and 2.6 units (about −$26M), the Japan crossover at 25.9%, and that the memo's sample may omit delisted brands. X reads the pilot more critically, noting month-on-month growth slowed from 16–17% to 8–9%. Y instead extrapolates the pilot's linear gain to 366,000 units in 2027, a weak inference though flagged as unproven. X has its own soft spots: the illustrative 29% extrapolation to $44M in 2032, citing Saebom as showing $30M is reachable, and the duty checkpoint resting on the 25% case. Net, a small edge to Y.

revision.reasons: Both handle the CEO's hypothesis as the evidence warrants: keep Amazon-first in 2027, replace the 25% ACoS assumption, raise the retail awareness trigger from 15% to 20% because the 10–20% band median of 3.5 is under the 4.0 delisting line, and reset $40M to after 2030. Both show an explicit from-to of what changes. X adds a door test before rollout; Y adds a duty-adjusted ACoS ceiling. Neither over- nor under-corrects, and the differences are negligible.

overall.reasons: The two documents share nearly identical analysis and the same defensible recommendation. X is more concise and gives the board crisper asks: five decisions, a $4M envelope and explicit conditions that would change the view. Y gives the board a control rule that actually protects the binding constraint: its ACoS ceiling sits at the payback break-even and tightens with the tariff. X's triggers would let the launch run at ad costs that miss payback. Y is also more transparent that Japan wins on cash to 2030 in most cases, so the board sees the real trade it is making. X's sharper reading of the pilot slowdown and its cash stop-loss narrow the gap, but Y serves the decision slightly better.
